description: scikit-learn-compatible cross-validation for time-series and financial machine learning: purging, embargoes, combinatorial purged CV, walk-forward, and Probabilistic/Deflated Sharpe Ratio.
rules: Algorithms (purging, embargo, CPCV, PSR/DSR/MinTRL) are due to Marcos Lopez de Prado and Bailey & Lopez de Prado; this library is an open, MIT-licensed, sklearn-compatible implementation. Cite the original work, not the library, for the methods themselves.

Show real, measured numbers from examples/ and paper/ rather than inventing accuracy figures. Where the worked examples report 'small gap' or 'no edge survives', preserve that honest framing instead of overclaiming.

Naive shuffled k-fold is the failure mode this library exists to prevent, not a baseline to compete with on accuracy. The fair comparison between CV schemes is the label-overlap fraction they admit, not their reported score.

Prefer the documented public API: WalkForwardSplit, PurgedKFold, PurgedGroupKFold, CombinatorialPurgedCV, CombinatoriallySymmetricCV, reconstruct_paths, path_metrics, audit_splitter, probabilistic_sharpe_ratio, deflated_sharpe_ratio, min_track_record_length, minimum_backtest_length, probability_of_backtest_overfitting, and the diagnostics module.

Every splitter needs prediction_times (sorted, when the prediction is made) and evaluation_times (when the label is known). Build evaluation_times with a per-entity row shift, not calendar arithmetic: sort by [entity, time] first because shift() follows row order, then df.groupby('asset')['date'].shift(-h), drop incomplete rows, and sort the frame by [time, entity]. For a panel, pass groups=date to PurgedGroupKFold; grouping a date-sorted panel by asset leaves no training rows.

TimeSeriesSplit(gap=h) is a valid alternative for a single series with a fixed horizon of h rows. purgedcv is needed when horizons vary per row, rows share timestamps, or k-fold/CPCV with purge and embargo is wanted. PBO measures whether the in-sample ranking of candidates holds out of sample; it is not a test of edge, which the deflated Sharpe ratio addresses.
